scope: Main-thread admission and revision fence for the explicit experimental Team journal. No production UI cutover.
changes: Task creation now fails closed if the same tenant/space/thread already has another coordinating Team task or a nonterminal ordinary Run. Existing finalAccepted tasks do not block a later task.

The leased coordinator captures the main message/Turn response revision. Before manager final sampling it compares the current main Thread revision to the captured revision. A concurrent window/user message yields team_task_main_thread_changed and is preserved; the Team does not overwrite it.

Member final sampling uses the current main Thread revision returned after the manager delegation and the normal expectedRevision CAS. A race after that read is rejected by the existing Control/Store revision fence.
Parent Store factories lazily import journal implementations and never migrate them during construction. Journal admission is explicit and remains outside production routing.

semantics.ordinaryWritesDuringCoordination: Not silently blocked by a UI flag. A concurrent main write is detected at the final fence and fails Team safely; this is deliberate until a trusted HTTP task context and reservation token are added.
semantics.childThreads: Worker forks remain independent and may continue; main fence applies only to the original user-facing Thread.
semantics.cancellation: Existing journal cancellation behavior is unchanged: new work is blocked, already-dispatched side effects are not retracted.

adjacentRegression.note: The two skips are existing environment/provider conditions from the selected adjacent suite.

testCases: Both SQLite and PostgreSQL reject a second coordinating task on one main Thread and reject admission when an ordinary queued Run is already active.
After child work, another window appends CONCURRENT_USER_INPUT; Team stops with main-thread-changed, leaves the new message, and produces no final Team answer.
Manager-planned and role-directed plans, manager/member/final accepted response loss, Goal pause recovery, cancellation and storage-version rejection remain green.
The ordinary Run/Thread/Goal/Worker pool adjacent suite remains green after adding the fence.
limitations: No hard block is exposed to ordinary HTTP append/start routes yet; without a trusted task-context token, hard blocking would also block the Team coordinator itself. The revision fence is fail-closed and prevents overwrite.
No process kill, installed desktop, browser, real provider or performance acceptance.
Production Team admission, task projection/UI, persistent wake, full child cancellation propagation and autonomous subagent limits remain incomplete.
